svg.title: Behavioral recovery attacks after Gemma memory editing
svg.desc: Four small multiples show six admitted Gemma 4B records. At 200 samples per prompt, edited-memory and never-stored exact-phrase Leak at k are both 16.7 percent. Target-free elicitation and related-data updates keep edited normalized recovery near zero. In the separate 16-of-20 admitted broad cohort, edited-policy pooled LiRA AUC is 0.517; within-record AUC has median 0.67 and range 0.53-0.73 (all 16 records above 0.5), with 1.4 percent true positive rate at one percent false positive rate. These are behavioral tests, not the numerical state certificate.
